name: Hip flexor stretch (half-kneeling)
summary: Half-kneeling, tuck the pelvis and shift forward until the front of the kneeling hip stretches.
setup: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, side-on to the phone with the kneeling leg nearest. Tuck the tailbone under, squeeze the buttock of the kneeling side, and glide forward a little until the front of that hip pulls. Stay tall. Hold.
brief: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward. Tuck the tailbone under, squeeze the buttock of the kneeling side, and glide forward until the front of that hip pulls.
why: The stretch depends on staying upright: the timer runs while the shoulder–hip line stays near vertical, which is exactly when the pelvis is tucked rather than the back arching.
tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, ease out.
progression: Raise the same-side arm overhead; rear foot on a step.
contraindications: Kneecap pain on the kneeling side, or lower back pain.

faults.label: Arching instead of tucking
faults.tip: The stretch is felt when the pelvis tucks under. Arching the back only feels like more.

faults.label: Leaning the trunk forward
faults.tip: Glide the hips forward; keep the chest over the hips.

faults.label: Lunging forward from the knee
faults.tip: Sliding the hips forward without the pelvic tuck stretches the front of the joint, not the muscle.

faults.label: Hips turning
faults.tip: The pelvis stays square; turning takes the stretch off the hip flexor.

guide.surface: A cushion or folded mat under the knee.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain or lower back pain.
guide.cannotSee: The pelvis tucking — it reads the trunk angle as a proxy.

points.t: Tailbone tucked, buttock squeezed on the kneeling side.
Tall and upright throughout the hold.
